newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set fresh closing record above 2,500.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set fresh closing record above 2,500.

text.p: French stocks rallied to historic highs on Thursday, propelling the blue-chip CAC-40 index above 2,500 points for the first time, after the Bank of France trimmed its key intervention rate.

The CAC-40 index finished up 38.05 points, or 1.54 percent, at 2,503.06, boosted by a 15.53 percent surge in shares of electrical engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom, which said it expected to show net income of 2.5 billion francs for 1996. Analysts were expecting a profit closer to 1.4 billion.
Traders said the bourse was underpinned by continuing gains on Wall Street.
The CAC-40 January futures contract closed 30.50 points higher at 2,495.50.
Volume was a heavy 10.65 billion francs, including 8.24 billion in the CAC-40 companies.
Within the first month of the year, the CAC index has pushed past the expectations of most market operators, who estimated in December that it would peak this year at around 2,450 points.
"They've just gone crazy," said one trader.
Alcatel shares led the rally, finishing up 70 francs at 523, after the market applauded its rebound from a 1995 loss of 25.6 billion francs due to massive restructuring charges.
Traders said Alcatel's performance stirred interest in lagging cyclical stocks.
PSA Peugeot Citroen shares, which have recently underperformed both the bourse and shares in rival Renault, closed up 5.28 percent at 598 francs.

Tyremaker Michelin's stock hit a year high of 322 francs before closing at 320.50, up 3.29 percent, after a series of positive recommendations by investment firms. The group this week denied speculation it may be planning a capital increase.
